newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen higher on firmer OTC prices.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen higher on firmer OTC prices.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open higher Wednesday in line with stronger prices in early over-the-counter (OTC) activity.
"We're seeing a short squeezing in the physical market. Higher prices for April but the rest of the curve is quiet," said a New York futures broker.

In OTC business, April Palo Verde (PV) reportedly traded as high as $15.30 a megawatt hour (MWh). May California-Oregon Border (COB) COB futures were discussed at $10.20-10.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) versus Tuesday's close of $10.25 and May PV at $14.50-14.70 against yesterday's settlement of $14.55.
Although April contracts expired mixed yesterday, the rest of complex finished mostly higher on firmer cash market prices and news of prolonged power plant outages in the Southwest.

The 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Palo Verde (PV) nuclear generating station in Arizona was restored to full production after its operation was scaled down to 61 percent of capacity to repair its low pressure feedwater system.
The 750 MW unit 2 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant was heard shut Tuesday for repairs. The status of the unit could not immediately be confirmed.
Southern California Edison said restart of the 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant has been delayed by another week to April 1 from tomorrow.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Washington will be shut Thursday, several weeks earlier than planned for maintenance due to ample hydropower in the region.

The market will keep watch when operators could begin ramping up the capacity on the Pacific Intertie transmission system by 20 percent to 6,250 MW. The capacity increase has been postponed due to the ongoin outage of a key 500 kilovolt segment of the line in Oregon.
In the Northwest, temperatures would average near normal along the coast and about 10 Fahrenheit degrees above normal in the extreme eastern area.
In the Southwest, readings would run as much as nine degrees F above normal in the northeast, but two to six degrees above normal everywhere else.
